import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 428

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/428](https://www.erdosproblems.com/428)
-/

open Nat Filter Set

namespace Erdos428

/--
The density ratio of set $A$ up to $n$ relative to the prime counting function $\pi(n)$.
-/
noncomputable def primeDensityRatio (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (A ∩ Icc 1 n).ncard / (primeCounting n)

/--
Is there a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that, for infinitely many $n$, all of $n-a$
are prime for all $a\in A$ with $0 < a < n$ and $$\liminf\frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{\pi(x)}>0?$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_428 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ A : Set ℕ,
      (∃ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a → a < n → (n - a).Prime) ∧
      liminf (fun n ↦ primeDensityRatio A n) atTop > 0 := by
  sorry

end Erdos428

reformulations.difference: Lean uses a real-valued Filter.liminf over natural-number cutoffs for the source's usual lower-limit expression as x tends to infinity. The real-valued operation has default values in unbounded cases, but those cases do not change this statement.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every admissible n, the map a ↦ n-a injects A ∩ [1,n-1] into the primes at most n-1. Hence primeDensityRatio A (n-1) ≤ 1 at arbitrarily large indices, while every ratio is nonnegative. These bounds make the real liminf valid and its positivity equivalent both to an eventual positive constant lower bound and to positivity of the extended-real liminf. Real cutoffs give the same limit because both counting functions depend only on floor(x). The full existential RHS equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as Review428.statement_equivalence, without sorryAx.
